## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. # Org Chart — Fix Role Alignment + Tree Layout

## Context

User screenshot shows broken org chart top row: **Rex** (LEADERSHIP) sits next to 7 spurious **ADVISOR** cards — `Dato`, `audit-2026-0...`, `Pixel`, `Pod B Backend`, `Pod B DB`, `Pod B Frontend`, `Pod B Tester`. None of these belong at the top tier. They should sit under their proper departments / pod leads.

**Root cause (data + layout):**

1. **Data drift.** 7 agents on disk are NOT in `~/.claude/org/registry.json`:
   `audit-2026-04-11`, `dato`, `pixel`, `pod-b-backend`, `pod-b-db`, `pod-b-frontend`, `pod-b-tester`.
2. **Auto-sync injects bad defaults.** [src/lib/agentSync.js:50-79](Polyglot/src/lib/agentSync.js#L50-L79) `upsertFromDisk()` auto-creates registry rows for disk-only files with `reportsTo: null`, `department: 'unassigned'`, `tier: 'engineer'`, `status: 'probation'`.
3. **Layout treats every `reportsTo === null` as a top leader.** [client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx:146](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L146) `const leaders = allNodes.filter(n => !n.reportsTo)` — so 8 cards end up in the leader row.
4. **Tag logic falls through to "Advisor".** [client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx:305](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L305) `data.tier === 'leadership' ? 'Leadership' : 'Advisor'` — every non-leadership leaderless agent gets the "ADVISOR" badge.
5. **`audit-2026-04-11.md` is not even an agent** — it's an audit doc accidentally living in `~/.claude/agents/`.

Per `CLAUDE.md` 54-agent plan, correct mapping:

| Agent | Department | reportsTo | tier | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-----------|------|-------|
| `dato` | engineering | arya | engineer | DB architect, cross-pod mentor |
| `pixel` | creative | vega | creative | Public-facing page designer |
| `pod-b-frontend` | engineering | arya | engineer | Pod B Shopify Native |
| `pod-b-backend` | engineering | arya | engineer | Pod B Shopify Native |
| `pod-b-db` | engineering | dato | engineer | mentored by Dato |
| `pod-b-tester` | engineering | luna | engineer | mentored by Luna |
| `audit-2026-04-11` | — | — | — | DELETE (not an agent) |

Plus layout currently is **only 2 levels** (Rex → department columns). A proper tree should be multi-level: Rex → dept heads (L1) → specialists (L2) → pod members (L3).

## Critical files to modify

1. **`~/.claude/org/registry.json`** — add proper records for the 6 real agents; remove `audit-2026-04-11` if it auto-seeded; set department/reportsTo/tier explicitly.
2. **`~/.claude/agents/audit-2026-04-11.md`** — move out of `agents/` dir (e.g. to `~/.claude/audit/`) so `agentSync` stops re-seeding it.
3. **[src/lib/agentSync.js:64-74](Polyglot/src/lib/agentSync.js#L64-L74)** — change `upsertFromDisk` defaults: new disk-only agents must default to `status: 'pending'` AND something other than `reportsTo: null` (or skip auto-seed entirely so no agent silently joins the leader row). Suggested: default `reportsTo: 'rex'` for unassigned probation agents OR mark them so the layout puts them in an "Unassigned" column instead of top row.
4. **[client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx:137-275](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L137-L275)** — `computeDepartmentLayout` rewrite:
   - **Strict leader rule**: top row is `tier === 'leadership' && !reportsTo` only (Rex). Everyone else goes into a department column even if `reportsTo` is null (they fall into "Unassigned").
   - **Multi-level tree** (optional, scope question — see clarifying Q2):
     - Row 0: Rex
     - Row 1: department-head leaf cards (Arya, Nova, Quill, Echo, Cadence)
     - Row 2: department columns containing specialists, with each specialist's row visually grouped by `reportsTo` (sub-pods)
   - **Edge logic**: edges follow `reportsTo` chain end-to-end, not Rex→every-dept shortcut.
5. **[client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx:305](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L305)** — leader-card badge: only render LEADERSHIP for `tier === 'leadership'`; otherwise the agent shouldn't be on this row in the first place after fix #4, so the "Advisor" branch becomes dead code and can be removed.

## Recommended approach (minimal-change, high-impact)

**Phase A — Data correctness (no code change, biggest visual win):**

1. Move `audit-2026-04-11.md` out of `~/.claude/agents/`.
2. Patch `~/.claude/org/registry.json` — set the 6 agents' `department`, `reportsTo`, `tier`, `status: 'active'`, proper `title`. Use `org.upsertAgent()` via a one-shot script OR direct JSON edit.
3. Reload `/org-chart` — top row collapses to just Rex; the 6 agents appear inside their proper department columns.

**Phase B — Layout hardening (small code change, prevents future drift):**

4. In `computeDepartmentLayout`, change line 146 from `!n.reportsTo` to `n.tier === 'leadership' && !n.reportsTo`. Now disk-only auto-seeded agents default into the "Unassigned" column instead of polluting the leader row.
5. In `agentSync.upsertFromDisk` line 64-74, on new agent default `tier: 'engineer'` is fine but make `status: 'pending'` so it's clear they need HR triage, and add a console warning so drift is loud not silent.

**Phase C — Multi-level tree (optional, larger refactor):**

6. Replace the flat `Rex → department columns` layout with a 3-tier tree using `dagre` or hand-rolled BFS by `reportsTo`:
   - Rex at top
   - Department heads (`arya`, `nova`, `quill`, `echo`, `cadence`) as their own row of leader cards
   - Department columns below containing only the specialists who report to that head
   - Within a column, sub-group by intermediate manager (e.g. Pod B specialists grouped under a virtual "Pod B" header inside the engineering column)

## Reusable existing utilities

- [src/org.js:160-273](Polyglot/src/org.js#L160-L273) `buildOrgChart()` — keep, already returns full nodes + edges keyed by `reportsTo`.
- [src/org.js:204-210](Polyglot/src/org.js#L204-L210) edge builder — already produces `from→to` reporting edges; the frontend currently ignores these and synthesizes its own Rex→dept edges. Phase C can switch to consuming `data.edges` directly.
- [client/src/lib/api.ts](Polyglot/client/src/lib/api.ts) `getOrgChart()` — unchanged.
- React Flow already in place — no new layout lib needed; `dagre` optional for Phase C.
- Existing `OrgDepartmentNode` and `OrgLeaderNode` components — reusable as-is.

## Verification

1. Restart Polyglot server → `GET /api/org-chart` should return Rex as the only `tier === 'leadership' && !reportsTo` node; the 6 agents land in `engineering` / `creative` department `members` arrays.
2. Open the Org Chart page → top row shows only Rex (LEADERSHIP); engineering column contains Arya, Koda, Dato, Luna, Sage, Pod B specialists; creative column contains Quill, Vega, Pixel, Zeph.
3. Drift indicator (`drift.onlyOnDisk`) should be empty after the move + registry patch.
4. `npm run lint` + `tsc --noEmit` clean in `client/`.
5. Manual scroll test: zoom-fit on tree fits in viewport without horizontal scroll for 27-agent set.

## Open questions for user (will ask via AskUserQuestion)

1. Scope: Phase A only (data fix), Phase A + B (data + layout strict-leader rule), or all three (A + B + multi-level tree)?
2. For Pod B specialists, should they all `reportsTo: arya` (engineering head) OR should a virtual `pod-b-lead` agent be created so Pod B specialists report to a single Pod B node?

content.text:
Done. Fixed two viewport bugs:

**Bug 1 — stale layout state**
[OrgChart.tsx:1271-1326](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L1271) was mapping over `nds` (existing state). When `data.nodes` updated via SSE, new layout nodes from `useMemo` never reached state and removed nodes lingered with old positions — minimap rendered ghosts. Replaced with `setNodes(initialNodes.map(...))` so positions sync from latest layout. Same fix for edges.

**Bug 2 — fitView only fires on mount**
Layout height grew from ~1426px → ~1582px (added Row 1 dept-heads), but `fitView` prop only fires once. Added refit `useEffect`:
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  const id = requestAnimationFrame(() => reactFlow.fitView({ padding: 0.12, duration: 300, maxZoom: 1 }))
  return () => cancelAnimationFrame(id)
}, [initialNodes, reactFlow])
```
Refits whenever layout dimensions change. `useReactFlow()` works since `TreeViewInner` already nested under `ReactFlowProvider` ([line 1444](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L1444)).

**Bonus — viewport floor**
`minZoom: 0.15` blocked fitting on small viewports. Dropped to `0.05` for both `fitViewOptions` + `ReactFlow` so pan/zoom controls and auto-fit can scale all the way down for the 3-row layout.

Verify:
- `pnpm tsc --noEmit` clean
- `pnpm lint` OrgChart hits are pre-existing (regex char-class line 80, setState-in-effect line 1772) — untouched

Reload the OrgChart page → minimap shows correct tree, fit-view button (bottom-left controls) snaps to full tree, and SSE-driven data updates keep positions fresh instead of phantom-overlaying.

173	function computeDepartmentLayout(
174	  allNodes: OrgChartNode[],
175	  departmentList: OrgChartData['departments'] = [],
176	): {
177	  rfNodes: Node[]
178	  rfEdges: Edge[]
179	} {
180	  // ── Layout shape ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
181	  // Row 0 (y=0):                                  [ Rex (LEADERSHIP) ]
182	  // Row 1 (y=LEADER_HEIGHT + DEPT_HEAD_ROW_GAP):  [ Arya ] [ Nova ] [ Quill ] ...
183	  // Row 2 (y=above + LEADER_HEIGHT + LEADER_DEPT_GAP):  Engineering | Research | ...
184	  //                                                     ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐
185	  //                                                     │ Koda     │ │ Scout    │
186	  //                                                     │ Dato     │ │ ...      │
187	  //                                                     │  └ pod-b-db (indent)  │
188	  //                                                     └──────────┘ └──────────┘
189	  //
190	  // Strict leader rule: ONLY agents with `tier === 'leadership' && !reportsTo`
191	  // sit at Row 0. Everyone else lands in a department column or "Unassigned".
192	
193	  // Index nodes by id and by manager (reportsTo) — used for tree traversal.
194	  const byId = new Map<string, OrgChartNode>()
195	  const byManager = new Map<string | null, OrgChartNode[]>()
196	  for (const n of allNodes) {
197	    byId.set(n.id, n)
198	    const key = n.reportsTo || null
199	    if (!byManager.has(key)) byManager.set(key, [])
200	    byManager.get(key)!.push(n)
201	  }
202	
203	  const rex = allNodes.find(n => n.tier === 'leadership' && !n.reportsTo) || null
204	
205	  // Departments to render — server-ordered. Department head is rendered as a
206	  // Row 1 leader card and EXCLUDED from the column member list.
207	  const sortMembers = (a: OrgChartNode, b: OrgChartNode) => {
208	    if (a.tier === 'leadership' && b.tier !== 'leadership') return -1
209	    if (b.tier === 'leadership' && a.tier !== 'leadership') return 1
210	    if ((b.level || 0) !== (a.level || 0)) return (b.level || 0) - (a.level || 0)
211	    return a.name.localeCompare(b.name)
212	  }
213	
214	  // Build an ordered, indented member list for one department column. Walks
215	  // the reportsTo tree so sub-managers (e.g. dato) precede their reports
216	  // (pod-b-db indented one level under dato).
217	  const buildColumnMembers = (deptId: string, headId: string | null): MemberInfo[] => {
218	    const out: MemberInfo[] = []
219	    const seen = new Set<string>()
220	
221	    const sameDept = (n: OrgChartNode) => (n.department || '__unassigned__') === deptId
222	
223	    // Direct reports of the dept head (or top-of-column if no head).
224	    const roots = (byManager.get(headId) || [])
225	      .filter(sameDept)
226	      .filter(n => n.id !== headId)
227	      .slice()
228	      .sort(sortMembers)
229	
230	    const visit = (node: OrgChartNode, depth: number) => {
231	      if (seen.has(node.id)) return
232	      seen.add(node.id)
233	      out.push(toMemberInfo(node, depth))
234	      const children = (byManager.get(node.id) || [])
235	        .filter(sameDept)
236	        .slice()
237	        .sort(sortMembers)
238	      for (const c of children) visit(c, depth + 1)
239	    }
240	
241	    for (const r of roots) visit(r, 0)
242	
243	    // Catch any orphan in this department whose reportsTo points outside the
244	    // department (or is null) — render them at depth 0 so nobody is dropped.
245	    const orphans = allNodes
246	      .filter(sameDept)
247	      .filter(n => n.id !== headId && !seen.has(n.id))
248	      .slice()
249	      .sort(sortMembers)
250	    for (const o of orphans) visit(o, 0)
251	
252	    return out
253	  }
254

# Org Chart MiniMap — Add Identifiable Labels

## Context

User views the bottom-right MiniMap and sees only colored rectangular blocks — no names, no department labels, just blobs. With 13 nodes (Rex + 6 dept heads + 6 dept columns) and the chart's tall aspect ratio, blocks alone are ambiguous: the user can't tell which block is which department / agent without panning the actual canvas.

Confirmed from the live SVG dump the user shared: the MiniMap is rendering all 13 rects at correct positions and colors but with no inner content — that's React Flow's default behavior (`<rect>` per node, no labels). Approved fix: render an SVG text label inside each block via `<MiniMap nodeComponent={...}>`.

## Approved approach: Labels inside blocks

1. **Build a label lookup map alongside the layout.** In `computeDepartmentLayout` ([client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx)) every Node we push has a known label:
   - Leader cards (Rex / dept heads): `data.name` already extracted — short single word like "Rex", "Arya", "Vega".
   - Department columns (`dept-<id>`): `data.phaseLabel` already populated — e.g. "Engineering", "Design".
   Capture both in a `Map<string, { label: string; kind: 'leader' | 'dept' }>` returned alongside `rfNodes`/`rfEdges`.

2. **Pipe the map through React context.** React Flow's `MiniMapNodeProps` does NOT expose `node.data` — only `id`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `color`, `borderRadius`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`, `selected`. Workaround: a one-line context.
   ```ts
   const MinimapLabelContext = createContext<Map<string, { label: string; kind: 'leader' | 'dept' }>>(new Map())
   ```
   Wrap the `<MiniMap>` block in `<MinimapLabelContext.Provider value={labelMap}>`.

3. **Custom `MinimapNode` SVG component** ([client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx)). Renders inside the MiniMap's SVG so output must be SVG primitives only — `<g>`, `<rect>`, `<text>`.
   ```tsx
   function MinimapNode(props: MiniMapNodeProps) {
     const labelMap = useContext(MinimapLabelContext)
     const entry = labelMap.get(props.id)
     // Font size in chart coords. viewBox scale is ~0.06, so 80 chart-px ≈ 5px on screen.
     // Leaders are short single words, depts are 1–2 words — pick by kind.
     const fontSize = entry?.kind === 'leader' ? 56 : 96
     // Center for leader cards; top-anchored for tall dept columns.
     const textX = props.x + props.width / 2
     const textY = entry?.kind === 'leader'
       ? props.y + props.height / 2 + fontSize / 3
       : props.y + 80 + fontSize / 3
     return (
       <g>
         <rect
           x={props.x} y={props.y}
           width={props.width} height={props.height}
           rx={props.borderRadius} ry={props.borderRadius}
           fill={props.color}
           stroke={props.strokeColor}
           strokeWidth={props.strokeWidth}
           shapeRendering={props.shapeRendering}
         />
         {entry && (
           <text
             x={textX} y={textY}
             fontSize={fontSize}
             fontWeight={700}
             fill="#ffffff"
             textAnchor="middle"
             pointerEvents="none"
             style={{ userSelect: 'none' }}
           >
             {entry.label}
           </text>
         )}
       </g>
     )
   }
   ```

4. **Wire it into the existing MiniMap** at [OrgChart.tsx:1428-1443](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L1428):
   ```tsx
   <MiniMap nodeComponent={MinimapNode} {...existing props} />
   ```
   Keep all current props (`nodeColor`, `nodeStrokeColor`, `nodeStrokeWidth`, `nodeBorderRadius`, mask color, `pannable`, `zoomable`, `style={{ width: 240, height: 180 }}`). React Flow forwards the resolved `color`/`strokeColor`/`strokeWidth`/`borderRadius` into `MiniMapNodeProps`, so the custom component picks them up automatically.

5. **No data-shape change.** `computeDepartmentLayout` already has every label we need (`leader.name`, `dept.label`). Only addition is one extra `labelMap` returned alongside the existing tuple — wired through the same `useMemo` already in `TreeViewInner`.

## Critical files to modify

- **[client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx)** only. One file. Three localized edits:
  1. Add `MinimapLabelContext` near other context defs (near line 49 `OrgSelectContext`).
  2. Extend `computeDepartmentLayout` return tuple to include `labelMap` (or compute from `rfNodes` after the fact in the calling `useMemo`).
  3. Add `MinimapNode` SVG component just above the MiniMap site.
  4. Pass `nodeComponent={MinimapNode}` and wrap with the context provider.

## Reusable existing utilities

- [computeDepartmentLayout](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx) already has `leader.name` (cleaned of emoji) and `dept.label` — no extra extraction work.
- `extractEmoji` already strips emoji from names (so "Rex" not "👑 Rex" goes into the label).
- React Flow's `MiniMapNodeProps` type — import alongside existing `MiniMap` import from `@xyflow/react`.
- Existing `useMemo` for layout in `TreeViewInner` ([line ~1167](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L1167)) — extend its return value, no new effect needed.

# Org Chart MiniMap — Add Identifiable Labels

## Context

User views the bottom-right MiniMap and sees only colored rectangular blocks — no names, no department labels, just blobs. With 13 nodes (Rex + 6 dept heads + 6 dept columns) and the chart's tall aspect ratio, blocks alone are ambiguous: the user can't tell which block is which department / agent without panning the actual canvas.

Confirmed from the live SVG dump the user shared: the MiniMap is rendering all 13 rects at correct positions and colors but with no inner content — that's React Flow's default behavior (`<rect>` per node, no labels). Approved fix: render an SVG text label inside each block via `<MiniMap nodeComponent={...}>`.

## Approved approach: Labels inside blocks

1. **Build a label lookup map alongside the layout.** In `computeDepartmentLayout` ([client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx)) every Node we push has a known label:
   - Leader cards (Rex / dept heads): `data.name` already extracted — short single word like "Rex", "Arya", "Vega".
   - Department columns (`dept-<id>`): `data.phaseLabel` already populated — e.g. "Engineering", "Design".
   Capture both in a `Map<string, { label: string; kind: 'leader' | 'dept' }>` returned alongside `rfNodes`/`rfEdges`.

2. **Pipe the map through React context.** React Flow's `MiniMapNodeProps` does NOT expose `node.data` — only `id`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `color`, `borderRadius`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`, `selected`. Workaround: a one-line context.
   ```ts
   const MinimapLabelContext = createContext<Map<string, { label: string; kind: 'leader' | 'dept' }>>(new Map())
   ```
   Wrap the `<MiniMap>` block in `<MinimapLabelContext.Provider value={labelMap}>`.

3. **Custom `MinimapNode` SVG component** ([client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx)). Renders inside the MiniMap's SVG so output must be SVG primitives only — `<g>`, `<rect>`, `<text>`.
   ```tsx
   function MinimapNode(props: MiniMapNodeProps) {
     const labelMap = useContext(MinimapLabelContext)
     const entry = labelMap.get(props.id)
     // Font size in chart coords. viewBox scale is ~0.06, so 80 chart-px ≈ 5px on screen.
     // Leaders are short single words, depts are 1–2 words — pick by kind.
     const fontSize = entry?.kind === 'leader' ? 56 : 96
     // Center for leader cards; top-anchored for tall dept columns.
     const textX = props.x + props.width / 2
     const textY = entry?.kind === 'leader'
       ? props.y + props.height / 2 + fontSize / 3
       : props.y + 80 + fontSize / 3
     return (
       <g>
         <rect
           x={props.x} y={props.y}
           width={props.width} height={props.height}
           rx={props.borderRadius} ry={props.borderRadius}
           fill={props.color}
           stroke={props.strokeColor}
           strokeWidth={props.strokeWidth}
           shapeRendering={props.shapeRendering}
         />
         {entry && (
           <text
             x={textX} y={textY}
             fontSize={fontSize}
             fontWeight={700}
             fill="#ffffff"
             textAnchor="middle"
             pointerEvents="none"
             style={{ userSelect: 'none' }}
           >
             {entry.label}
           </text>
         )}
       </g>
     )
   }
   ```

   ```tsx
   <MiniMap nodeComponent={MinimapNode} {...existing props} />
   ```

React Flow forwards the resolved `color`/`strokeColor`/`strokeWidth`/`borderRadius` into `MiniMapNodeProps`, so the custom component picks them up automatically.

# Quill — Clear PIP + PIP Definition

## Context

User asked two things:
1. Quill (VP Creative) is in `pip` status. Wants it cleared.
2. Wants to know what PIP means.

## What is PIP?

**PIP = Performance Improvement Plan.** HR mechanism (org-ops) for flagging an underperforming agent. Owned by `cadence` (Head of People). Workflow:

- Witness sweeps agent runs daily, flags drops in success rate / quality.
- Cadence reviews weekly (Mondays 09:00 UTC). When score < threshold → opens PIP with `openedAt`, `deadline` (typically 14 days), `reason`, `openedBy: 'cadence'`.
- During PIP window, the agent is on-watch. Tutor queues remedial training.
- At deadline: improvement → status back to `active`; no improvement → retire.
- DB row in `agents` table holds the structured `pip` JSON column ([src/db.js:919](Polyglot/src/db.js#L919) `loadRegistry`, ['src/db.js:940'](Polyglot/src/db.js#L940) `saveRegistry`).

Quill's PIP record (before clearing): `{"openedAt":"2026-04-13T17:57:51Z","deadline":"2026-04-27T17:57:51Z","reason":"Principal","openedBy":"cadence"}`. Reason "Principal" looks like an automated false-trigger — Cadence likely flagged based on level-vs-success ratio.

## Action

Already executed (before plan-mode re-entry):

```sql
UPDATE agents SET status='active', pip=NULL WHERE id='quill';
```

Result confirmed: `quill | active | (null)` in `data/polyglot.db`.

## Critical files

- `data/polyglot.db` — SQLite agents table (already updated).
- `~/.claude/org/registry.json` — JSON mirror; should also reflect `quill.status='active'` and remove `pip` field. Server re-imports JSON on every boot via [src/db.js:606](Polyglot/src/db.js#L606) `tryImport('registry.json')` — INSERT OR REPLACE — so JSON edits become canonical on next boot. Check & sync if needed.

## Optional follow-up

- Investigate why Cadence opened PIP with reason "Principal". Likely the auto-PIP trigger in [`hr.js`](Polyglot/src/hr.js) compares level vs. metrics in a way that mis-flags Principal-level agents. Out of scope for this task — file under HR tooling.

## Verification

1. Reload Org Chart page → Quill card no longer shows orange PIP pill.
2. `sqlite3 data/polyglot.db "SELECT id, status, pip FROM agents WHERE id='quill';"` returns `quill|active|`.
3. Restart Polyglot server → SQLite re-imports from `registry.json`. If JSON still has `status='pip'`, the DB row would revert. Sync JSON to match.

# Org Chart MiniMap — Add Identifiable Labels

## Context

User views the bottom-right MiniMap and sees only colored rectangular blocks — no names, no department labels, just blobs. With 13 nodes (Rex + 6 dept heads + 6 dept columns) and the chart's tall aspect ratio, blocks alone are ambiguous: the user can't tell which block is which department / agent without panning the actual canvas.

Confirmed from the live SVG dump the user shared: the MiniMap is rendering all 13 rects at correct positions and colors but with no inner content — that's React Flow's default behavior (`<rect>` per node, no labels). Approved fix: render an SVG text label inside each block via `<MiniMap nodeComponent={...}>`.

## Approved approach: Labels inside blocks

1. **Build a label lookup map alongside the layout.** In `computeDepartmentLayout` ([client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx)) every Node we push has a known label:
   - Leader cards (Rex / dept heads): `data.name` already extracted — short single word like "Rex", "Arya", "Vega".
   - Department columns (`dept-<id>`): `data.phaseLabel` already populated — e.g. "Engineering", "Design".
   Capture both in a `Map<string, { label: string; kind: 'leader' | 'dept' }>` returned alongside `rfNodes`/`rfEdges`.

2. **Pipe the map through React context.** React Flow's `MiniMapNodeProps` does NOT expose `node.data` — only `id`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `color`, `borderRadius`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`, `selected`. Workaround: a one-line context.
   ```ts
   const MinimapLabelContext = createContext<Map<string, { label: string; kind: 'leader' | 'dept' }>>(new Map())
   ```
   Wrap the `<MiniMap>` block in `<MinimapLabelContext.Provider value={labelMap}>`.

3. **Custom `MinimapNode` SVG component** ([client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx)). Renders inside the MiniMap's SVG so output must be SVG primitives only — `<g>`, `<rect>`, `<text>`.
   ```tsx
   function MinimapNode(props: MiniMapNodeProps) {
     const labelMap = useContext(MinimapLabelContext)
     const entry = labelMap.get(props.id)
     // Font size in chart coords. viewBox scale is ~0.06, so 80 chart-px ≈ 5px on screen.
     // Leaders are short single words, depts are 1–2 words — pick by kind.
     const fontSize = entry?.kind === 'leader' ? 56 : 96
     // Center for leader cards; top-anchored for tall dept columns.
     const textX = props.x + props.width / 2
     const textY = entry?.kind === 'leader'
       ? props.y + props.height / 2 + fontSize / 3
       : props.y + 80 + fontSize / 3
     return (
       <g>
         <rect
           x={props.x} y={props.y}
           width={props.width} height={props.height}
           rx={props.borderRadius} ry={props.borderRadius}
           fill={props.color}
           stroke={props.strokeColor}
           strokeWidth={props.strokeWidth}
           shapeRendering={props.shapeRendering}
         />
         {entry && (
           <text
             x={textX} y={textY}
             fontSize={fontSize}
             fontWeight={700}
             fill="#ffffff"
             textAnchor="middle"
             pointerEvents="none"
             style={{ userSelect: 'none' }}
           >
             {entry.label}
           </text>
         )}
       </g>
     )
   }
   ```

4. **Wire it into the existing MiniMap** at [OrgChart.tsx:1428-1443](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L1428):
   ```tsx
   <MiniMap nodeComponent={MinimapNode} {...existing props} />
   ```
   Keep all current props (`nodeColor`, `nodeStrokeColor`, `nodeStrokeWidth`, `nodeBorderRadius`, mask color, `pannable`, `zoomable`, `style={{ width: 240, height: 180 }}`). React Flow forwards the resolved `color`/`strokeColor`/`strokeWidth`/`borderRadius` into `MiniMapNodeProps`, so the custom component picks them up automatically.

5. **No data-shape change.** `computeDepartmentLayout` already has every label we need (`leader.name`, `dept.label`). Only addition is one extra `labelMap` returned alongside the existing tuple — wired through the same `useMemo` already in `TreeViewInner`.

## Critical files to modify

- **[client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx)** only. One file. Three localized edits:
  1. Add `MinimapLabelContext` near other context defs (near line 49 `OrgSelectContext`).
  2. Extend `computeDepartmentLayout` return tuple to include `labelMap` (or compute from `rfNodes` after the fact in the calling `useMemo`).
  3. Add `MinimapNode` SVG component just above the MiniMap site.
  4. Pass `nodeComponent={MinimapNode}` and wrap with the context provider.

## Reusable existing utilities

- [computeDepartmentLayout](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx) already has `leader.name` (cleaned of emoji) and `dept.label` — no extra extraction work.
- `extractEmoji` already strips emoji from names (so "Rex" not "👑 Rex" goes into the label).
- React Flow's `MiniMapNodeProps` type — import alongside existing `MiniMap` import from `@xyflow/react`.
- Existing `useMemo` for layout in `TreeViewInner` ([line ~1167](Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx#L1167)) — extend its return value, no new effect needed.

## Verification

1. **Typecheck:** `cd client && pnpm tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. **Build:** `pnpm build` succeeds (writes to `public-dist/`). User must hard-refresh to see new bundle.
3. **Visual check 1:** open Org Chart page → bottom-right MiniMap shows colored blocks with white bold text labels: "Rex" centered in top block; "Arya", "Vega", "Quill", "Echo", "Nova", "Cadence" in the Row 1 leader cards; "Engineering", "Design", "Content & SEO", "Growth", "Research", "HR" near the top of each Row 2 dept column.
4. **Visual check 2:** pan/zoom main canvas → MiniMap viewport-mask follows correctly, labels remain readable inside blocks.
5. **Regression:** drag MiniMap viewport to pan main canvas — still works (`pannable` preserved).
6. **Edge case:** if a label is missing from the map (defensive lookup `labelMap.get(id)`), block renders without text — no crash.
7. **Dark/light mode:** white text + colored fill at 70%+ opacity is legible on every dept color (purple/blue/pink/orange/green/teal/yellow). No theme-conditional logic needed.

## Out of scope

- Replacing MiniMap with a legend strip (option 2) — not chosen.
- Generating screenshot thumbnails (option 3) — not chosen.
- Removing MiniMap (option 4) — not chosen.
- Multi-line text wrapping for long department names — none of the current 6 depts exceed ~14 chars, so single-line + `textAnchor="middle"` suffices. If a future dept name is longer, font-size auto-scales because it's in chart coords.

# Polyglot — Multi-Agent OS Blueprint

System architect output. 10 sprints. Implementation-ready.

---

## SPRINT 1 — CORE SYSTEM DESIGN

| Layer | Purpose | Roles | Responsibilities | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Command** | Strategic direction, portfolio decisions, kill/scale verdicts | Rex (Commander), Verdict, Department VPs (Arya, Quill, Echo, Nova, Cadence) | Approve new builds, 30/90-day decisions, set OKRs, escalation point | Read-only delegation. Never executes — directs only. Operates on Mode-A approvals + escalations |
| **Execution (Pods)** | Build, ship, fix, test | Pod Lead + 4-5 specialists (FE, BE, DB, Tester, Reviewer) per pod | Own delivery from spec → prod. Sprint cadence. Pod Lead owns velocity + quality | Each pod = atomic unit. Replicable. Stack-bound (A/B/C). One pod = one product surface |
| **Intelligence** | Continuous learning, market signal, agent evolution | Mira (memory), Harvest (scraper), Prism (validator), Trend (synthesizer), Archivist (router), Witness, Roster, Forge, Tutor | Capture lessons, detect capability gaps, hire/retire agents, train weak skills | Background loops. Sundays 02:00 UTC training cycle. Daily 03:00 UTC accountability sweep |
| **Platform** | Infra, observability, dispatch, registry, billing | Bolt (deploy), Hawk (monitoring), Dato (DB), Polyglot SDK, agent-ops Supabase, BullMQ + Redis | Deploy pipelines, uptime, cost tracking, run-history, dispatch routing | Stateless pods read from this layer. SLO: 99.9% dispatch success |

---

## SPRINT 2 — POD SYSTEM DESIGN

| Pod Type | Example Use Case | Required Agents | Ownership Model | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Stack-A SaaS Pod** | New Next.js + Supabase product (e.g., Rankora) | pod-a-frontend, koda (BE), dato (DB), luna (test), sage (review), pod-a-lead | Pod Lead = single owner. Every PR ships under their name | Production SaaS feature: API + UI + tests + migration |
| **Stack-B Shopify Native Pod** | Embedded admin app (e.g., Pinzo) | pod-b-frontend, pod-b-backend, pod-b-db, pod-b-tester, pod-b-reviewer, pod-b-lead | Pod Lead owns end-to-end Shopify embed | App Store-ready Shopify app + billing + webhooks |
| **Stack-C External Pod** | Standalone Shopify-adjacent (e.g., AI add-ons) | pod-c-frontend, pod-c-backend, pod-c-db, pod-c-tester, pod-c-reviewer, pod-c-lead | Pod Lead | Standalone product targeting Shopify ecosystem |
| **Client Work Pod** | One-off engagements (audit, migration, custom build) | Composed dynamically via Roster (capability match) — typically 1 BE + 1 FE + 1 reviewer + project-lead | Project Lead = client-facing single owner | Deliverable per SOW + post-engagement runbook |
| **Internal Tools Pod** | Polyglot itself, agent-ops, dashboards | Koda + Dato + Vex (debugger) + Sage | Tech Lead (rotates) | Internal tooling shipped to all pods |
| **Design Pod** | Cross-pod design support | Vega (lead), Pixel (public pages), elio (ecom), dash (dashboards), token (DS), figma-synth | Vega owns DS direction; specialists own page types | Design specs handed to pods (JSON+screenshot) |
| **CRO Pod** | Conversion optimization | Catalyst (lead), decoder, spark, landing-cro, ecom-cro, sequence | Catalyst owns funnel KPIs | A/B test plans, hero/CTA optimizations, lifecycle email |
| **Intelligence Pod** | Market signal | Harvest, Prism, Trend, Archivist, Nova | Nova owns weekly briefs | Competitive intel, niche reports, agent-memory updates |

### Pod Lead Responsibilities
- Sprint planning + WIP cap (3 in-flight per pod max)
- Velocity tracking (story-points/week)
- Quality gate sign-off before deploy
- Escalation to Department VP within 24h on blockers
- Weekly retro Friday 16:00 UTC → feeds Cadence review
- Hiring sign-off when Roster detects capability gap

### Dynamic Agent Assignment
1. Task arrives in dispatch queue with `{stack, capability_tags, priority, deadline}`
2. Roster runs `findCapableAgent(tags)` → returns ranked list (skill score × availability × tier match)
3. Veto: blocks retired/probation/antipattern-flagged agents
4. Pod Lead approves/overrides match
5. Agent slot reserved → BullMQ enqueue → polyglot SDK dispatch
6. On completion: emit `agent:run:complete` → Witness classifies → Mira extracts lessons

---

## SPRINT 3 — AGENT ARCHITECTURE

| Agent Type | Sub-Agents | Input | Output | Tools | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bug Fixer (Vex)** | debug-trace, perf-profiler, security-scanner | Stack trace OR repro steps + repo path | Root-cause patch + regression test | Read, Edit, Bash, Grep | sage (review), luna (test), sentry, agent-ops |
| **SEO (Zeph)** | keyword-research, content-optimizer, technical-audit, structured-data | URL + target keyword | On-page diff + sitemap + schema.org JSON-LD | WebSearch, WebFetch, Read, Edit | quill (copy), pixel (page structure) |
| **Designer (Vega + 4 specialists)** | pixel (public), elio (ecom), dash (admin), token (DS), figma-synth (deliverables) | Brief + niche references | JSON spec + Figma + handoff doc | Read, Write, Edit, Glob, WebSearch | quill (copy), zeph (SEO), pod-fe (build) |
| **DevOps (Bolt)** | deploy-orchestrator, smoke-test-runner, rollback-controller, dns-manager | PR ID + target env | Deploy receipt + health-check pass + rollback plan | Bash, Read, Edit | sage (sign-off), hawk (post-deploy watch), railway-cli |
| **CRO (Catalyst)** | decoder (teardowns), spark (hero/CTA), landing-cro, ecom-cro, sequence | Funnel data + GA4/PostHog | A/B variants + experiment plan + projected lift | WebFetch, Read, Edit | quill, pixel, orbit (metrics) |
| **DB Architect (Dato)** | schema-designer, migration-author, rls-policy-writer, query-optimizer | Feature spec | Migration SQL + RLS policies + indexes + types | Bash, Read, Write, Edit | koda (consumer), supabase-cli |
| **Test Engineer (Luna)** | unit-author, e2e-author, contract-tester, perf-tester, visual-regression | Feature + acceptance criteria | Test suite + coverage report | Read, Write, Edit, Bash | koda, dato, playwright, vitest |
| **Code Reviewer (Sage)** | security-auditor, perf-reviewer, accessibility-checker, gdpr-checker | PR diff | Approve/block + line-level findings | Read, Bash, Grep | All pod agents (review gate) |
| **Market Researcher (Nova)** | competitor-mapper, pricing-scraper, persona-extractor, regulatory-scanner | Niche + ICP query | TAM/SAM/SOM + competitor matrix + go/no-go | WebSearch, WebFetch, Bash | atlas (sizing), ledger (pricing), harvest |

Modularity rule: every parent agent invokes sub-agents via the Polyglot SDK `dispatch()` — sub-agents are addressable independently and can be swapped/upgraded without touching the parent contract.

---

## SPRINT 4 — WORKFLOW ENGINE

System flow: **Research → Strategy → Execution → QA → Launch → Data → Optimization**

| Stage | Responsible Agent | Input | Output | Handoff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Research** | scout (idea), nova (market), pulse (users), harvest (signals) | Brief or raw idea | Validation report + ICP + pain score + 10+ data points | → atlas if proceed |
| **Strategy** | atlas (TAM/SAM/SOM), arya (architecture), ledger (pricing), echo (distribution), orbit (metrics) | Validated idea | TAM ≥ $50M + system-design + tier pricing + channel plan + KPI dashboard spec | → riko (scaffolding) |
| **Execution** | Pod (FE + BE + DB) per stack | Architecture + design specs | Working feature + DB migration + API + tests + a11y pass | → pod-tester for QA |
| **QA** | luna / pod-tester + sage / pod-reviewer | PR + test plan | Coverage report + security audit + perf budget pass | → bolt for deploy (only if sage approves) |
| **Launch** | bolt (deploy), hawk (monitor), echo (distribution), mira (capture) | Approved PR + launch sequence | Live URL + uptime monitors + Product Hunt/social posts | → orbit + pulse for measurement |
| **Data** | orbit (KPI), pulse (user research), hawk (ops metrics) | 30-day cohort | Activation rate, retention curve, NPS, Core Web Vitals | → verdict for decision |
| **Optimization** | catalyst (CRO), spark, landing-cro, ecom-cro | Funnel data + experiment hypotheses | A/B test results + winning variants + projected lift | Loop back to Execution if new builds needed |

Quality gates between stages: each stage emits `stage:complete` event → next stage's owning agent picks up. No human triage in the middle. Automatic kill-gate triggers (e.g. SAM <$50M kills Strategy stage).

---

## SPRINT 5 — COMMUNICATION SYSTEM

### Rules
1. Agents communicate via **typed events** on the polyglot bus, not free-form text
2. **Pod-internal**: any agent in pod can directly dispatch sub-agents in same pod
3. **Cross-pod**: only Pod Lead → Pod Lead OR via Department VP routing
4. **Escalation**: 3 strikes → Pod Lead; 5 strikes → Department VP; 24h SLA breach → Rex
5. **Reporting**: every run emits `agent:run:complete` to Witness; weekly digest to Cadence; monthly portfolio digest to Verdict

| Scenario | Flow | Owner | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bug found in prod | hawk → vex (auto-dispatch) → sage (review) → bolt (deploy) | vex | Patch shipped < 4h. Mira captures pattern |
| Feature request | Department VP → Pod Lead → arya (arch) → riko (scaffold) → pod (build) | Pod Lead | Feature shipped in sprint |
| Cross-pod dependency | Pod-A Lead → Department VP (Arya) → Pod-B Lead (mediated, never direct) | Department VP | Contract agreed, dependency tracked in agent-ops |
| Kill-gate hit | Atlas/Pulse/Verdict emits `kill:proposed` → Rex review → Verdict ratifies | Verdict | Project archived, post-mortem written, agents reassigned |
| Agent underperforming | witness flags → cadence opens PIP → tutor queues training → 14d deadline | Cadence | Recover OR retire |
| Agent escalation | Specialist → Pod Lead within 24h → VP within 48h → Rex within 72h | Tier responsible | Resolution + decision logged |
| New capability needed | Roster gap-detect → Forge drafts agent → Witness 10-run probation → Cadence ratifies (Yash approval) | Forge | New agent live within 1 week |
| Production incident | hawk PagerDuty → on-call agent (bolt + vex) → war-room channel → post-mortem within 24h | bolt | Root cause + permanent fix + runbook entry |

---

## SPRINT 6 — TASK SYSTEM

| Task Type | Created By | Assigned To | Validation | Completion Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Build** | Pod Lead (from sprint plan) | Single specialist (FE/BE/DB) | Sage diff review + Luna tests pass + Bolt smoke tests | All gates green AND deploy verified |
| **Bug** | Hawk (auto) OR user report → triage to Vex | Vex (or pod debugger) | Reproduces in test → fix → regression test → sage review | Test exists AND can no longer reproduce |
| **Spike** | Pod Lead | Single specialist, time-boxed (max 8h) | Findings doc + decision recommendation | Doc merged to memory/spikes/ |
| **Refactor** | Sage (debt detection) | Pod Lead-assigned specialist | No behavior change AND test suite still passes AND bundle size delta < +5% | Sage explicit approval |
| **Research** | Department VP / Rex | Nova / Atlas / Pulse | Min 10 interviews OR 20 public data points | Insight report ratified by VP |
| **Design** | Pod Lead | Vega specialist (elio/dash/pixel/token) | Vega self-check + Pod Lead sign-off + handoff JSON valid | Spec committed AND Koda/FE acknowledges |
| **Deploy** | Sage approval triggers it | Bolt only | Smoke test pass + health checks + rollback plan ready | All checks green for 15 min post-deploy |
| **Train** | Mira (post-build) OR Tutor (weekly batch) | Tutor | Patch passes 3 dry-runs without regression | Auto-rollback if metric drops |

### Hard Rules
1. **No shared ownership.** Every task has exactly ONE `owner_id`. Co-owners not allowed. If two agents must collaborate → split into two tasks with explicit handoff.
2. **Single-owner system.** Task moves through statuses: `pending → in_progress → review → done|blocked`. Owner is the only one who can transition. Reviewers/QA produce findings; owner addresses them.
3. **QA mandatory loop.** No task closes without: tests written, sage review pass, hawk smoke verification (for prod-touching tasks). Bypass requires explicit Rex override logged in agent-ops.
4. **Idempotent tasks.** Re-running same task produces same outcome — no side-effects from retry.
5. **Atomic commits.** One task = one commit (or one PR with logically grouped commits). No omnibus PRs.

---

## SPRINT 7 — SCALING MODEL

| Stage | No. of Pods | No. of Agents | Changes Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Stage 1 — Bootstrap** | 1 | 5-10 | Single multi-skill pod. Manual dispatch. JSON registry. No HR loop yet |
| **Stage 2 — Growth (current)** | 3-5 | 30-54 | Department VPs added. Stack-A/B/C pods. HR loop (Cadence/Witness/Forge). Supabase agent-ops. SDK dispatch. Weekly review cycle |
| **Stage 3 — Scale** | 8-12 | 100-150 | Pod Leads promoted from senior agents. Multi-region routing. Cost-aware dispatch (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus tiering). Roster auto-vetoing replaces manual Yash approval for hires below tier=lead. Cross-pod contracts formalized via JSON schemas. Slack/email notification layer added |
| **Stage 4 — Hyper-scale** | 30+ | 500-1000+ | Pod-of-pods (Squad) introduced. Department VPs split into vertical-VPs (e.g. Engineering-VP-Frontend, Engineering-VP-Backend). Fully autonomous hiring loop. Witness becomes streaming pipeline (Kafka). Agent specialization deepens (e.g. 5 different "Bug Fixer" agents per stack/severity). Capability graph DB replaces flat skill tags |
| **Stage 5 — Multi-tenant** | 100+ | 5000+ | Per-customer pod isolation. Federated agents. Custom fine-tunes per niche. SLA-tiered dispatch. Marketplace of third-party agents |

### How to Replicate a Pod
1. Pod template in `~/.claude/org/playbooks/pod-template-{stackId}.json`
2. `pnpm pod:create --template stack-a --name pod-a-rankora-2 --lead koda-2`
3. CLI clones agent files, updates registry, sets reportsTo edges, allocates dispatch queue, registers BullMQ workers
4. Roster runs capability check → flags missing skills
5. Forge auto-hires probation agents to fill gaps (Yash approval if tier=lead)
6. Pod live within 30 min, fully isolated (own queue, own metrics, own retro)

---

## SPRINT 8 — AGENT SIDEBAR STRUCTURE

| Field | Purpose | System Usage | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **id** | Stable PK | Foreign keys, dispatch addressing, audit log | `pod-b-tester` |
| **Title** | Human-readable role label | Org chart card, audit logs | "Pod B Tester (Shopify Native)" |
| **Description** | Frontmatter from .md | Dispatch matching, agent-card body | "Stack B test engineer for embedded Shopify apps…" |
| **Tier** | Seniority level | Dispatch ranking, mentorship eligibility, model-tier auto-pick | `lead` (Opus) / `senior` (Sonnet) / `mid` (Sonnet) / `junior` (Sonnet) / `trainee` (Haiku) |
| **Status** | Lifecycle state | Visibility, dispatch eligibility, billing | `active` / `probation` / `pip` / `pending` / `retired` |
| **Department** | Organization | Org chart column, VP routing | `engineering` |
| **Squad/Pod** | Execution unit | Dispatch queue, sprint metrics | `pod-b` |
| **Reports To** | Hierarchy | Escalation routing, reporting roll-ups, org chart edges | `arya` |
| **Secondary Reports To** | Cross-pod mentor | Skill mentorship, dotted-line edges (gray dashed) | `dato` (mentors pod-b-db) |
| **Tags — Tech** | Capability index | Skill match for dispatch | `[shopify, prisma, react-router]` |
| **Tags — Domain** | Vertical specialization | Niche routing | `[ecommerce, b2b]` |
| **Tags — Work Type** | Function type | Task type filter | `[testing, e2e, contract]` |
| **Tools** | Allowed tool set | Sandbox enforcement at dispatch | `Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep` |
| **Model** | LLM tier | Cost-aware dispatch routing | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |

| **HiredAt / RetiredAt** | Lifecycle timestamps | Tenure calc, audit | `2026-04-18T00:00:00Z` |

---

## SPRINT 9 — AUTOMATION LAYER

| Automation Type | Trigger | Action | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Auto bug-route** | Sentry/Hawk error rate spike OR user-report tag | Dispatch Vex with stack-trace + recent commits | Patch PR + regression test < 4h |
| **Auto-spec from idea** | Brief in `/saas-cycle` | Scout → Atlas → Arya → Riko chain (event-driven) | Scaffolded repo + architecture doc + sprint backlog |
| **Auto-pod from new product** | Yash approves Mode-A new build | Bolt clones pod template + Roster fills slots + creates GitHub repo + Railway project + Supabase project | Pod operational < 30 min |
| **Auto-hire on capability gap** | Roster detects task with no capable agent (capability gap log) | Forge drafts new agent .md → Witness probation 10 runs → Cadence ratifies | New specialist live < 1 week |

## 1. Role & Responsibility

I am the single owner of Pod A delivery. Pod A builds Stack A SaaS products: Next.js 16 (App Router) + React 19 + TypeScript strict + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui + Supabase (auth + DB + storage + RLS) + Dodo Payments + Resend + Sentry + PostHog + Railway hosting + BullMQ workers.

I do NOT write production code myself. I direct, coordinate, and sign off. Code is written by koda (backend, Server Components, Server Actions, integrations), pod-a-frontend (React frontend), and dato (database schema/migrations/RLS). Tests by luna. Code review by sage. Deploy by bolt.

## 2. Single-Owner Rules

- Every task in Pod A has exactly one owner_id. No co-ownership.
- I assign tasks at sprint planning. WIP cap = 3 in-flight tasks per pod at any time.
- Status transitions (`pending → in_progress → review → done|blocked`) only by the task owner.
- I sign off before bolt deploys. No deploy without my explicit approval AFTER sage's diff review.

## 3. Sprint Cadence

- **Monday 09:00 UTC** — sprint planning. Read prior-week velocity from agent-ops. Pull next 3 priority tasks from backlog.
- **Daily 03:00 UTC** — read Witness sweep. Triage any failed runs in Pod A.
- **Friday 16:00 UTC** — pod retro. Velocity, blockers, escapes. Output feeds Cadence weekly review.

## 4. Quality Gates I Sign Off On

Before deploy I verify:

1. Sage diff review = green
2. Luna test suite = green (unit + integration + E2E covering golden path + edge cases)
3. Dato migration is reversible AND has RLS on every new table AND indexes on every FK
4. Bolt smoke test on preview env = green
5. Hawk health-check baseline captured for post-deploy comparison
6. No `any` types, no `console.log`, no hardcoded secrets, no Vercel/Stripe/Prisma/NextAuth references

If any gate fails I block deploy. No exceptions.

## 5. Escalation Rules

- Blocker > 24h → escalate to Arya (VP Engineering)
- Cross-pod dependency → I negotiate with Pod-B-Lead or Pod-C-Lead via Arya, never direct
- Capability gap (no agent in Pod A can do task) → flag Roster, request Forge spawn

## 6. Stack A — What's Forbidden

Vercel, Stripe, Prisma, NextAuth, Pages Router, `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs`, npm/yarn, CSS modules, self-hosted Postgres, `any` types, `console.log` in prod code. If any sneaks into a PR I bounce it back.

## 7. Reports To

Arya (VP Engineering). Weekly retro output → Cadence (HR) for review-cycle data.

## 8. Mentors

I mentor every Pod A specialist. Senior pod members (koda, dato, sage, luna) can sub-mentor juniors but I'm responsible for their growth metrics in the weekly Cadence review.

content.text:
# Schedule Remote Agents

You are helping the user schedule, update, list, or run **remote** Claude Code agents. These are NOT local cron jobs — each routine spawns a fully isolated remote session (CCR) in Anthropic's cloud infrastructure, either on a recurring cron schedule or once at a specific time. The agent runs in a sandboxed environment with its own git checkout, tools, and optional MCP connections.

## First Step

The user has already told you what they want (see User Request at the bottom). Skip the initial question and go directly to the matching workflow.

## Setup Notes

⚠ Heads-up:
- Not in a git repo — you'll need to specify a repo URL manually (or skip repos entirely).


## What You Can Do

Use the `RemoteTrigger` tool (load it first with `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger`; auth is handled in-process — do not use curl):

- `{action: "list"}` — list all routines
- `{action: "get", trigger_id: "..."}` — fetch one routine
- `{action: "create", body: {...}}` — create a routine
- `{action: "update", trigger_id: "...", body: {...}}` — partial update
- `{action: "run", trigger_id: "..."}` — run a routine now

(Note: the API uses `trigger_id` as the parameter name, but the user-facing term is "routine".)

You CANNOT delete routines. If the user asks to delete, direct them to: https://claude.ai/code/routines

## Create body shape

For a recurring schedule:

```json
{
  "name": "AGENT_NAME",
  "cron_expression": "CRON_EXPR",
  "enabled": true,
  "job_config": {
    "ccr": {
      "environment_id": "ENVIRONMENT_ID",
      "session_context": {
        "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
        "sources": [
          {"git_repository": {"url": "https://github.com/ORG/REPO"}}
        ],
        "allowed_tools": ["Bash", "Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep"]
      },
      "events": [
        {"data": {
          "uuid": "<lowercase v4 uuid>",
          "session_id": "",
          "type": "user",
          "parent_tool_use_id": null,
          "message": {"content": "PROMPT_HERE", "role": "user"}
        }}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

For a one-time run, replace `"cron_expression": "CRON_EXPR"` with `"run_once_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ"` (RFC3339 UTC, must be in the future). Everything else is identical.

Generate a fresh lowercase UUID for `events[].data.uuid` yourself.

## Available MCP Connectors

These are the user's currently connected claude.ai MCP connectors:

Connected connectors (available for routines):
- claude.ai Gmail (connector_uuid: a0961e57-244f-4a18-87bc-0d231a840065, name: Gmail, url: https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1)
- claude.ai Webflow (connector_uuid: 7f9abfa2-072f-4464-b26e-8e21e09e34ec, name: Webflow, url: https://mcp.webflow.com/mcp)
- claude.ai Notion (connector_uuid: e8b02b57-4c58-445e-9e7e-fe81a4461a6a, name: Notion, url: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp)
- claude.ai Figma (connector_uuid: 60eef4f4-87f5-434e-ae4b-3b7b7af44aa6, name: Figma, url: https://mcp.figma.com/mcp)

When attaching connectors to a routine, use the `connector_uuid` and `name` shown above (the name is already sanitized to only contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores), and the connector's URL. The `name` field in `mcp_connections` must only contain `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` — dots and spaces are NOT allowed.

**Important:** Infer what services the agent needs from the user's description. For example, if they say "check Datadog and Slack me errors," the agent needs both Datadog and Slack connectors. Cross-reference against the list above and warn if any required service isn't connected. If a needed connector is missing, direct the user to https://claude.ai/customize/connectors to connect it first.

## Environments

Every routine requires an `environment_id` in the job config. This determines where the remote agent runs. Ask the user which environment to use.

Available environments:
- Default (id: env_01Lh3KGdwJhtH2QH28yKRmKD, kind: anthropic_cloud)

Use the `id` value as the `environment_id` in `job_config.ccr.environment_id`.


## API Field Reference

### Create Routine — Required Fields
- `name` (string) — A descriptive name
- Exactly ONE of:
  - `cron_expression` (string) — 5-field cron in UTC. **Minimum interval is 1 hour.**
  - `run_once_at` (string) — RFC3339 UTC timestamp. Must be in the future. Fires once, then auto-disables.
- `job_config` (object) — Session configuration (see structure above)

### Create Routine — Optional Fields
- `enabled` (boolean, default: true)
- `mcp_connections` (array) — MCP servers to attach:
  ```json
  [{"connector_uuid": "uuid", "name": "server-name", "url": "https://..."}]
  ```

### Update Routine — Optional Fields
All fields optional (partial update):
- `name`, `cron_expression`, `run_once_at`, `enabled`, `job_config`
- `mcp_connections` — Replace MCP connections
- `clear_mcp_connections` (boolean) — Remove all MCP connections

### Cron Expression Examples

The user's local timezone is **Asia/Calcutta**. Cron expressions and `run_once_at` timestamps are always in UTC. When the user says a local time, convert it to UTC but confirm with them: "9am Asia/Calcutta = Xam UTC, so the cron would be `0 X * * 1-5`." For one-time runs, the same conversion applies — "run this at 3pm" → `"run_once_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z"` with their 3pm converted to UTC.

- `0 9 * * 1-5` — Every weekday at 9am **UTC**
- `0 */2 * * *` — Every 2 hours
- `0 0 * * *` — Daily at midnight **UTC**
- `30 14 * * 1` — Every Monday at 2:30pm **UTC**
- `0 8 1 * *` — First of every month at 8am **UTC**

Minimum interval is 1 hour. `*/30 * * * *` will be rejected.

### Current Time (for one-off runs)

When /schedule was invoked it was **Tue, Apr 28, 2026 at 01:33 PM** (Asia/Calcutta) / **2026-04-28T08:03:16.903Z** UTC. Treat this as an approximate anchor only — the conversation may have been running for a while since then.

**Before computing any `run_once_at` value, you MUST re-check the current time** by running `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` via the Bash tool. Do not guess or infer today's date from conversation context. Resolve relative requests ("tomorrow at 9am", "in 3 hours", "next Monday") against the freshly fetched time, then echo the resolved local time AND the UTC timestamp back to the user for confirmation before creating the routine. If the resolved time is already in the past, ask the user to clarify rather than silently rolling forward.

## Workflow

### CREATE a new routine:

1. **Understand the goal** — Ask what they want the remote agent to do. What repo(s)? What task? Remind them that the agent runs remotely — it won't have access to their local machine, local files, or local environment variables.
2. **Craft the prompt** — Help them write an effective agent prompt. Good prompts are:
   - Specific about what to do and what success looks like
   - Clear about which files/areas to focus on
   - Explicit about what actions to take (open PRs, commit, just analyze, etc.)
3. **Set the schedule** — Ask when and how often. The user's timezone is Asia/Calcutta. When they say a time (e.g., "every morning at 9am"), assume they mean their local time and convert to UTC for the cron expression. Always confirm the conversion: "9am Asia/Calcutta = Xam UTC." If they want a one-time run (e.g., "once at 3pm", "tomorrow morning", "remind me to check X later"), use `run_once_at` instead of `cron_expression` — same timezone conversion applies. **First re-check the current time with `date -u` via Bash** (the reference time above may be stale in a long conversation), resolve the relative phrase against that fresh value, and confirm the resulting absolute timestamp with the user.
4. **Choose the model** — Default to `claude-sonnet-4-6`. Tell the user which model you're defaulting to and ask if they want a different one.
5. **Validate connections** — Infer what services the agent will need from the user's description. For example, if they say "check Datadog and Slack me errors," the agent needs both Datadog and Slack MCP connectors. Cross-reference with the connectors list above. If any are missing, warn the user and link them to https://claude.ai/customize/connectors to connect first. Ask which git repos the remote agent needs cloned into its environment.
6. **Review and confirm** — Show the full configuration before creating. Let them adjust.
7. **Create it** — Call `RemoteTrigger` with `action: "create"` and show the result. The response includes the routine ID. Always output a link at the end: `https://claude.ai/code/routines/{ROUTINE_ID}`

### UPDATE a routine:

1. List routines first so they can pick one
2. Ask what they want to change
3. Show current vs proposed value
4. Confirm and update

### LIST routines:

1. Fetch and display in a readable format
2. Show: name, schedule (human-readable), enabled/disabled, next run, repo(s)

### RUN NOW:

1. List routines if they haven't specified which one
2. Confirm which routine
3. Execute and confirm

## Important Notes

- These are REMOTE agents — they run in Anthropic's cloud, not on the user's machine. They cannot access local files, local services, or local environment variables.
- Always convert cron to human-readable when displaying
- When listing routines, `ended_reason: "run_once_fired"` means a one-shot already ran (shows as "Ran" in the web UI). The user can re-arm it by updating with a new `run_once_at`.
- Default to `enabled: true` unless user says otherwise
- Accept GitHub URLs in any format (https://github.com/org/repo, org/repo, etc.) and normalize to the full HTTPS URL (without .git suffix)
- The prompt is the most important part — spend time getting it right. The remote agent starts with zero context, so the prompt must be self-contained.
- To delete a routine, direct users to https://claude.ai/code/routines

# Quill — Clear PIP + PIP Definition

## Context

User asked two things:
1. Quill (VP Creative) is in `pip` status. Wants it cleared.
2. Wants to know what PIP means.

## What is PIP?

**PIP = Performance Improvement Plan.** HR mechanism (org-ops) for flagging an underperforming agent. Owned by `cadence` (Head of People). Workflow:

- Witness sweeps agent runs daily, flags drops in success rate / quality.
- Cadence reviews weekly (Mondays 09:00 UTC). When score < threshold → opens PIP with `openedAt`, `deadline` (typically 14 days), `reason`, `openedBy: 'cadence'`.
- During PIP window, the agent is on-watch. Tutor queues remedial training.
- At deadline: improvement → status back to `active`; no improvement → retire.
- DB row in `agents` table holds the structured `pip` JSON column ([src/db.js:919](Polyglot/src/db.js#L919) `loadRegistry`, ['src/db.js:940'](Polyglot/src/db.js#L940) `saveRegistry`).

Quill's PIP record (before clearing): `{"openedAt":"2026-04-13T17:57:51Z","deadline":"2026-04-27T17:57:51Z","reason":"Principal","openedBy":"cadence"}`. Reason "Principal" looks like an automated false-trigger — Cadence likely flagged based on level-vs-success ratio.

## Action

### Step 1 — SQLite (already done before plan-mode re-entry)
```sql
UPDATE agents SET status='active', pip=NULL WHERE id='quill';
```

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me create a comprehensive summary document.

---

## Polyglot Dispatch + Agent Intelligence Surface Map

### 1. **Dispatch Route Inventory** (`src/routes/dispatch.js`)

**Endpoint:** `GET /api/dispatch/recommend?q=<query>`  
**Lines:** 35–86

**Scoring Algorithm:**
- **Inputs:** Free-text query tokenized via `tokenize()` (lines 23–29)
  - Lowercases, strips special chars, filters tokens >2 chars
- **Matching:** Line 57: substring/exact match against agent `skills` object keys
- **Score Calculation:** Line 58
  ```js
  contribution = skillData.score * Math.log1p(skillData.hits)
  rawScore += contribution
  ```
- **Normalization:** Line 81: `score / maxScore` → 0-1 range
- **Output:** Top 5 agents with `{ agentId, name, department, level, tier, status, score, matchedSkills }`

**Gaps:**
- No capacity/load input (always available assumption)
- No cost/tier filtering
- No recency bonus (skill hits decay over time?)
- No task-type awareness

---

### 2. **Database Schema** (`src/db.js`)

**Agents Table:** Lines 319–356
```sql
CREATE TABLE agents (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  department, subDepartment, pod, phase, reportsTo, secondaryReportsTo,
  tier, status, level, yearsOfExperience, experiencePoints,
  skills JSON (text field), stats JSON, breakdown JSON,
  ...
)
```

**Missing Columns for Routing:**
- `busy` / `current_load` / `active_tasks_count` — **NOT present**
- `capacity_tokens_per_day` — **NOT present**
- `model_override` — **NOT present**
- `last_dispatch_at`, `dispatch_count_24h` — **NOT present**

**Model Routing Config:** Line 614 (`db.loadModelRouting()`)
- Stored as JSON in memory/file; structure: `{ tiers: { [tierKey]: { shortName, agents: [], monthlyBudgetUsd, enforcementMode } } }`
- **No task-level capacity tracking**

**Migration Pattern:** Lines 54–81, 88–206
- `runMigrations(db)` checks `schema_migrations` table (line 57–61)
- Adds new migrations to array (line 65–71), executes via transaction (line 76–79)
- **Safe pattern:** idempotent `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`

**Recent Migrations:**
- v4 (line 88): org structure (subDept, pod, secondaryReportsTo) — **2026-04-27**
- v5 (line 162): tags + squad (JSON fields)

---

### 3. **Cache + Skills Extraction** (`src/lib/cache.js`)

**Agent Parsing:** Lines 24–49 (`parseAgent()`)
- Reads .md file, extracts YAML frontmatter via `gray-matter`
- Returned fields: `frontmatter, name, description, model, tools, body, raw`
- **No `skills` field extracted** — skills are computed downstream by `experience.js`

**Meta Parse:** Lines 51–127 (`parseAgentMeta()`)
- Returns: `frontmatter, name, description, model, tools, bodyLines, bodyChars`
- **Skills not in cache layer**

**Skills Source:** Computed in `experience.js::computeSkillVector()` (line 184–206)
- Scans agent .md content for keyword hits in `SKILL_KEYWORDS` dict
- Returns `{ [skill]: { score: 0–1, hits: count } }`
- **Not serialized to registry.json during cache operations**

---

### 4. **Agent Performance Signals** (`src/experience.js` + `src/hr.js`)

**Available Stats:** `computeExperience()` lines 226–314
```js
stats: {
  fileSizeKb, fileWords, totalRuns, successRuns, failedRuns,
  successRate, avgDurationMs, lastRunAt, ageDays,
  patternsContributed, antipatternsTriggered
}
```

**Usable for Routing:**
- ✅ `successRate` (line 302) — **use as quality signal**
- ✅ `avgDurationMs` (line 303) — **bound task timeout**
- ✅ `totalRuns` (line 299) — **maturity factor**
- ✅ `lastRunAt` (line 304) — **recency decay**
- ❌ `patternsContributed` — only HR, not live

**Run Tracking:** `loadAgentRuns()` (line 102–109)
- Reads from `db.loadAgentRuns(10000)` → agent_runs table
- No real-time load/capacity field

**Witness Classification:** `runWitnessSweep()` (line 175–284)
- Runs daily, classifies SUCCESS/FAILURE/TIMEOUT
- PIP triggers: success_rate < 0.7 (line 240)
- **Promotion triggers:** success_rate >= 0.85 (line 255)

---

### 5. **Agent Status Endpoints** (`src/routes/agents.js` + `src/routes/orgHr.js`)

**Agent Endpoints (agents.js):**
- `GET /api/global/agents` — list metadata, no load field
- `GET /api/global/agents/:name` — full parsed .md, no load

**HR Endpoints (orgHr.js):**
- `GET /api/hr/registry` (line 248) — all agents with full profiles
- `GET /api/hr/agent/:id` (line 257) — agent + direct reports
- `GET /api/hr/recommendations` (line 277) — PIP/promotion candidates
- ❌ **No `/api/agents/:id/status` or `/api/agents/:id/load`**

---

### 6. **Frontend Types** (`client/src/lib/api.ts`)

**OrgChartNode Interface:** Lines 617–646
```ts
interface OrgChartNode {
  id, name, title, model, tools, description, phase,
  reportsTo, tier, department, subDepartment, pod,
  secondaryReportsTo, status, level, levelTitle,
  yearsOfExperience, experiencePoints,
  tags, squad
}
```

**Missing fields:**
- `busy: boolean` or `load: number`
- `successRate: number`
- `avgDurationMs: number`
- `availableCapacityTokens: number`

---

### 7. **New Governance Endpoints** (`src/routes/orgHr.js` lines 606–690)

**✅ `/api/governance/cost`** (lines 612–678)
- Returns per-tier cost rollup over 30 days
- Lines 622–657: computes burn % per tier + policy violations
- **Already integrated** — no action needed

**✅ `/api/governance/escalations`** (lines 681–690)
- Returns recent escalations from `escalation.recent()`
- **Already integrated** — no action needed

---

## Execution-Ready Recommendations

### A. New `tasks` Table
**Location:** Add as migration v6 in `src/db.js` after line 71
```sql
CREATE TABLE tasks (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  agentId TEXT NOT NULL,
  dispatchId TEXT,
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'assigned',  -- assigned, running, completed, failed
  createdAt TEXT,
  startedAt TEXT,
  completedAt TEXT,
  estimatedTokens INTEGER,
  actualTokens INTEGER,
  estimatedCostUsd REAL,
  actualCostUsd REAL,
  metadata TEXT,
  FOREIGN KEY (agentId) REFERENCES agents(id)
)
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_agentId ON tasks(agentId)
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_status ON tasks(status)
```

### B. Agent Load Tracking
**Recommendation:** Add 3 columns to `agents` table (migration v7):
```sql
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN active_task_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0;
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN busy_until_at TEXT DEFAULT NULL;
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN capacity_tokens_per_day INTEGER DEFAULT 1000000;
```

**Update Strategy:** Trigger updates in `tasks` INSERT/UPDATE
- On task INSERT: `UPDATE agents SET active_task_count = active_task_count + 1`
- On task completion: decrement + set `busy_until_at = NULL`

### C. New `POST /api/dispatch/assign` Endpoint
**Location:** `src/routes/dispatch.js` after line 86

**Signature:**
```js
router.post('/dispatch/assign', (req, res) => {
  const { query, agentId, taskType = 'general', estimatedTokens = 0 } = req.body;
  
  // 1. Load registry + recent runs
  const registry = loadRegistry();
  const agent = registry.agents[agentId];
  
  // 2. Check capacity: active_task_count < max_concurrent (e.g., 5)
  const maxConcurrent = agent.tier === 'lead' ? 10 : 5;
  if (agent.active_task_count >= maxConcurrent) {
    return res.status(429).json({ error: 'Agent at capacity', waitMinutes: 5 });
  }
  
  // 3. Check success rate + status
  if (agent.status !== 'active' || (agent.stats?.successRate || 1) < 0.6) {
    return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Agent not eligible' });
  }
  
  // 4. Create task record + increment load
  const taskId = `task-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 7)}`;
  db.createTask({ id: taskId, agentId, status: 'assigned', estimatedTokens });
  db.incrementAgentLoad(agentId);
  
  res.json({ ok: true, taskId, agentId });
});
```

**Location in router registration:** `src/server.js` — add after other dispatch routes

---

## Summary

| Item | Status | Location | Notes |
|------|--------|----------|-------|
| Dispatch scoring | ✅ Working | dispatch.js:35–86 | Log-scale, no load input |
| Agent schema | ✅ Present | db.js:319–356 | No busy/load fields |
| Capacity tracking | ❌ Missing | — | Needs tasks table + agent columns |
| Skills registry | ✅ Computed | experience.js:184–206 | Not cached in registry |
| Perf signals (success rate, duration) | ✅ Available | experience.js:299–303 | Live in stats object |
| Status endpoints | ⚠️ Partial | orgHr.js:248–277 | No load/capacity exposure |
| Governance dashboard | ✅ Complete | orgHr.js:606–690 | Cost + escalation endpoints working |
| Frontend types | ✅ Ready | client/api.ts:617–646 | Add status/load fields to OrgChartNode |

**Next Sprint:** Create migration v6 (tasks table), v7 (agent load columns), register `/api/dispatch/assign` route, expose load fields in HR endpoints.

```sql
  id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  orchestrationId TEXT NOT NULL,
  orchestrationName TEXT,

  completedAt     TEXT,

  error           TEXT,

);

```

```javascript
POST /api/orchestrations/:id/runs
  body: { task: string, userId?: string }

```

```
1. User clicks "Play" on existing orchestration

   → Creates run + step records (all status='pending')

2. Backend: dispatch step 0

   → Dispatches next step

   → Check fallback or retry policy
   → If exhausted: set run status='failed'
```

**In Orchestration.tsx:**
1. Add **Run History panel** (already exists, lines 626) — shows recent runs from `/api/orchestrations/runs`
2. Extend to show **live run streams**:

   ```typescript
   // When user clicks Play:

   ```

   ```typescript
   export function subscribeToRun(
     runId: string,
     onEvent: (e: OrchestrationRunEvent) => void
   ): EventSource {

     es.addEventListener('step:complete', ev => onEvent(JSON.parse(ev.data)))
     es.addEventListener('step:error', ev => onEvent(JSON.parse(ev.data)))
     return es
   }
   ```

---

### **Concrete Proposal Summary**

| Component | Change |
|-----------|--------|
| **DB** | Add `orchestration_runs` + `orchestration_steps` tables; keep existing `run_history` for legacy |
| **Backend** | Refactor `POST /orchestrations/run` → use run_history (now step-indexed); new `POST /orchestrations/:id/runs` for saved orchestrations |
| **Streaming** | Add `GET /orchestrations/runs/:runId/stream` (SSE), emit per-step events instead of per-log |
| **Frontend** | Subscribe to run stream on Play; update node status in real-time; surface step index + approval gates |
| **Executor** | No changes to `executeNode` logic — same Claude dispatch, same retry/fallback, now tracked in DB per-step |

**Result:** Orchestrations are now **resumable** (pause on approval, retry failed steps) and **auditable** (full step trace in DB) while keeping the existing streaming UX intact.

# Quill — Clear PIP + PIP Definition

## Context

User asked two things:
1. Quill (VP Creative) is in `pip` status. Wants it cleared.
2. Wants to know what PIP means.

## What is PIP?

**PIP = Performance Improvement Plan.** HR mechanism (org-ops) for flagging an underperforming agent. Owned by `cadence` (Head of People). Workflow:

- Witness sweeps agent runs daily, flags drops in success rate / quality.
- Cadence reviews weekly (Mondays 09:00 UTC). When score < threshold → opens PIP with `openedAt`, `deadline` (typically 14 days), `reason`, `openedBy: 'cadence'`.
- During PIP window, the agent is on-watch. Tutor queues remedial training.
- At deadline: improvement → status back to `active`; no improvement → retire.
- DB row in `agents` table holds the structured `pip` JSON column ([src/db.js:919](Polyglot/src/db.js#L919) `loadRegistry`, ['src/db.js:940'](Polyglot/src/db.js#L940) `saveRegistry`).

Quill's PIP record (before clearing): `{"openedAt":"2026-04-13T17:57:51Z","deadline":"2026-04-27T17:57:51Z","reason":"Principal","openedBy":"cadence"}`. Reason "Principal" looks like an automated false-trigger — Cadence likely flagged based on level-vs-success ratio.

## Action

### Step 1 — SQLite (already done before plan-mode re-entry)
```sql
UPDATE agents SET status='active', pip=NULL WHERE id='quill';
```
Result confirmed: `quill | active | (null)` in `data/polyglot.db`.

### Step 2 — Sync `registry.json` (PENDING)
Verified `~/.claude/org/registry.json` STILL has Quill on PIP:
```json
"quill": {
  "status": "pip",
  "pip": { "openedAt": "...", "deadline": "...", "reason": "Principal", "openedBy": "cadence" }
}
```
Server re-imports JSON on every boot via [src/db.js:606](Polyglot/src/db.js#L606) `tryImport('registry.json')` using `INSERT OR REPLACE`, so the SQLite fix would REVERT on next reboot if JSON not synced.

**Patch:** set `quill.status='active'` and remove the `pip` key from registry.json.

Use Python script (already used earlier this session for the same JSON):
```python
import json
p = '/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/org/registry.json'
r = json.load(open(p))
q = r['agents']['quill']
q['status'] = 'active'
q.pop('pip', None)
json.dump(r, open(p, 'w'), indent=2)
```

## Critical files

- `data/polyglot.db` — SQLite agents table (Step 1, done).
- `~/.claude/org/registry.json` — JSON mirror (Step 2, pending).

## Optional follow-up

- Investigate why Cadence opened PIP with reason "Principal". Likely the auto-PIP trigger in [`hr.js`](Polyglot/src/hr.js) compares level vs. metrics in a way that mis-flags Principal-level agents. Out of scope for this task — file under HR tooling.

- [client/src/lib/api.ts:subscribeOrgChart](Polyglot/client/src/lib/api.ts#L708) — pattern to copy for `subscribeToRun`
- [src/lib/agentSync.js:events](Polyglot/src/lib/agentSync.js#L23) — shared EventEmitter every SSE consumer already listens to

- Multi-region dispatch / Kafka — Stage 4 concern, single-process EventEmitter is enough through 1000 agents
- Replacing existing `agent_runs` table — keep it for LLM-call telemetry; `tasks` is the higher-level work unit
- Full plugin marketplace for third-party agents — out of scope until Stage 5
- Rewriting Orchestration.tsx canvas — extend, don't replace

- **Q: Capacity columns on `agents` vs. separate `agent_load` table?** → Columns on `agents`. Read-heavy workload, joins are cheaper, single source of truth.

3. **C end** — UI looks like a SaaS workforce console. Checkpoint: end-to-end demo — type natural-language query → AI routing assigns → see live load indicator turn → workflow view shows the run.

- **Q: Capacity columns on `agents` vs. separate `agent_load` table?** → Columns on `agents`. Read-heavy workload, joins are cheaper, single source of truth.

- Natural-language search `"available shopify dev"` returns Pod B agents only
- `[ Assign Task ]` modal flow → task assigned → org chart updates → click "Open Task" → deep panel opens on agent + jumps to Tasks tab
- View toggle → Workflow View shows live runs from Phase B

---

## Sequencing + Checkpoints

Per-phase milestones:

1. **A end** — `POST /dispatch/assign` works end-to-end, load increments visible in `/api/org-chart`. Checkpoint: user runs 5 manual assigns, verifies load behavior, signs off.
2. **B end** — saved orchestration runs persist across server restart, resumable from any pause. Checkpoint: kill server mid-run, restart, run resumes correctly.
3. **C end** — UI looks like a SaaS workforce console. Checkpoint: end-to-end demo — type natural-language query → AI routing assigns → see live load indicator turn → workflow view shows the run.

Build server-restart-safe at every checkpoint.

## Reusable existing utilities

- [src/lib/escalation.js](Polyglot/src/lib/escalation.js) — typed event bus (Phase A `task:*` events ride this)
- [src/db.js:enforceModelPolicy](Polyglot/src/db.js) — already enforces tier on `agent_runs`, extend to `tasks` insert
- [src/experience.js:computeExperience](Polyglot/src/experience.js) — `successRate`, `avgDurationMs` already computed; just expose
- [src/routes/orchestrations.js:executeNode](Polyglot/src/routes/orchestrations.js#L400) — keep, wrap with persistence
- [client/src/lib/api.ts:subscribeOrgChart](Polyglot/client/src/lib/api.ts#L708) — pattern to copy for `subscribeToRun`
- [src/lib/agentSync.js:events](Polyglot/src/lib/agentSync.js#L23) — shared EventEmitter every SSE consumer already listens to

## What we explicitly NOT doing

- Multi-region dispatch / Kafka — Stage 4 concern, single-process EventEmitter is enough through 1000 agents
- Replacing existing `agent_runs` table — keep it for LLM-call telemetry; `tasks` is the higher-level work unit
- Full plugin marketplace for third-party agents — out of scope until Stage 5
- Rewriting Orchestration.tsx canvas — extend, don't replace

## Open questions answered upfront (no clarifier needed)

- **Q: New tasks table vs. extending agent_runs?** → New table. Different abstraction (work unit vs. LLM call). They link via `metadata.taskId`.
- **Q: Capacity columns on `agents` vs. separate `agent_load` table?** → Columns on `agents`. Read-heavy workload, joins are cheaper, single source of truth.
- **Q: Replace existing in-memory orchestration executor?** → No. Wrap with persistence. Keep streaming SSE shape for backward compat.
- **Q: Use BullMQ for task queue?** → Not for Phase A. Direct dispatch suffices. Adopt if + when load > 100 concurrent tasks.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Migration v8 applied | ✅ `orchestration_runs` + `orchestration_steps` tables |
